original_question: Let M be the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. Is the derivative map f -> (M f)' continuous from W^{1,1}(R) to L^1(R)? In other words, whenever f_j converges to f in W^{1,1}(R), must the derivatives of the centered maximal functions converge in L^1(R) as well?
target_in_paper: Question 12 in Section 7.1 (Endpoint study): the open continuity problem for the derivative-level map f ↦ (Mf)' for the one-dimensional centered classical Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct problem almost exactly: it is one-dimensional, centered, concerns the classical Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator M, asks about continuity at the derivative level, uses the correct source and target spaces W^{1,1}(R) and L^1(R), and phrases continuity via convergence f_j → f in W^{1,1}(R). This is precisely the centered counterpart singled out in the paper as Question 12.
missing_details: The operator should be made explicit: for x in R, Mf(x) := sup_{r>0} (1/(2r)) ∫_{x-r}^{x+r} |f(y)| dy, i.e. the supremum of centered interval averages of |f|.
The derivative (Mf)' should be identified as the weak derivative (equivalently, the a.e. derivative when defined in this one-dimensional Sobolev/BV setting).
The paper works throughout with real-valued functions, so that ambient convention should be stated if one wants the question to be fully paper-faithful and stand-alone.
It helps to specify that this is the centered classical continuous-setting endpoint continuity question, not the uncentered, fractional, discrete, BV, or higher-dimensional variant.
refined_question: Let M be the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on real-valued functions, defined by Mf(x) := sup_{r>0} (1/(2r)) ∫_{x-r}^{x+r} |f(y)| dy for x in R. Is the map f ↦ (Mf)' continuous from W^{1,1}(R) to L^1(R)? That is, if f_j, f ∈ W^{1,1}(R) and ||f_j - f||_{W^{1,1}(R)} → 0, must ||(Mf_j)' - (Mf)'||_{L^1(R)} → 0?
justification: In arXiv:1912.04625, the nearest official formulation is not a theorem or conjecture but the survey’s open Question 12. Section 1 fixes the centered maximal operator and Sobolev notation; Section 3 explains the endpoint p=1 derivative-level regularity problem; then Section 7.1 proves the uncentered one-dimensional continuity statement in Theorem 7.2 and immediately asks for the centered analogue as Question 12. Table 1 later records exactly this slot—centered classical maximal operator, continuous setting, continuity—as OPEN. Also, the labels Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 do not occur in this paper, so Question 12 is the closest official paper formulation matching your draft.
